title: Colimits of sections from preserved local fiber cocones
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, colimits and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $q:E\to S$ be a categorical fibration of quasicategories (an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with prescribed source), assumed locally cocartesian, meaning that its pullback along each edge $\Delta^1\to S$ is a cocartesian fibration. For $s\in S$ let $E_s$ be its fiber, and for $a:s\to t$ let $a_!:E_s\to E_t$ be local transport, determined by that edge pullback. Let $\Gamma(q)=\operatorname{Fun}_S(S,E)$ be the infinity-category of coherent sections, with transformations and higher simplices over the identity on $S$. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe.

Let $K$ be a small simplicial set and $P:K\to\Gamma(q)$ a diagram. Suppose that for every $s\in S$ its evaluation $P_s:K\to E_s$ has a colimiting cocone $c_s:P_s\to\Delta_K l_s$, and that $a_!c_s$ is colimiting in $E_t$ for every edge $a:s\to t$ of $S$. Then there exists a colimiting cocone $C:P\to\Delta_K L$ in $\Gamma(q)$ whose evaluation at every $s$ is equivalent, as a cocone on $P_s$, to $c_s$. Under these hypotheses a cocone on $P$ is colimiting in $\Gamma(q)$ if and only if all its evaluations are colimiting in the respective fibers. Only the specified fiber cocones and their local transports are assumed to be colimiting; no other colimits in the fibers or in $S$ are assumed, and $q$ need not be a globally cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), dual of Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp. 362-363; combine with Higher Topos Theory (2009), Proposition 4.3.1.10 (locally cocartesian fiber criterion) and Proposition 4.3.1.5(4) (base change to the section fiber), printed pp. 262, 265-266. Online sources read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra and Higher Topos Theory in literature/. No Stacks tag covers coherent section colimits.

proof.text: Put $J=K^{\triangleright}$. The opposite-category and opposite-join identifications of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4), applied to [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], give the right-join comparison with coherent cocones, including equivalence after fixing the boundary diagram. Choose for each $s$ a join representative $x_s:J\to E_s$ of $c_s$, with boundary exactly $P_s$ and induced cocone equivalent to $c_s$. Colimitness is unchanged by this equivalence, by the cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The same is true after applying each $a_!$. Consequently [lem-coef-local-fiber-relative-colimit-test] says that $x_s$, viewed in $E$, is a $q$-colimit diagram. This uses precisely the supplied cocones and their outgoing local transports, including the identity edge.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.3.1.10; right-join counterpart of Kerodon 4.6.4.9, via opposite duality.

proof.text:
Form the quasicategories
$$X=\operatorname{Fun}(J,E),\qquad T=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)}\operatorname{Fun}(J,S),$$
and the corner map $r:X\to T$, $u\mapsto(u|_K,qu)$. Since $q$ is a categorical fibration, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-initial-corner] makes $r$ an isofibration and makes every $x_s$ an $r$-initial vertex. Transposing $P$ gives $F:K\times S\to E$ with $qF=\operatorname{pr}_S$. The map $h:S\to T$ has components the transpose $s\mapsto P_s$ of $F$ and the constant-$J$ diagram at $s$. Thus $r(x_s)=h(s)$ exactly. The exponential isofibration assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], first for $\varnothing\subset S$, shows that $r^S:\operatorname{Fun}(S,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ is an isofibration. Its strict fiber $Z$ over $h$ is a quasicategory: an inner-horn lifting problem in $Z$ is a problem for $r^S$ over the constant simplex at $h$. Likewise $\Gamma(q)$ is a quasicategory, as the fiber of $q^S$ over $\mathrm{id}_S$.

Construct $f:S\to X$ over $h$ with $f(s)=x_s$. Start on the simplicial subset generated by the vertices of $S$, assigning their degeneracies by the simplicial rules. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to its inclusion in $S$. Suppose the lift is defined on the preceding skeleton. For a nondegenerate $d$-simplex $\sigma$ outside this subset, $d>0$ and its boundary already has a lift. Its first vertex is the prescribed $r$-initial object $x_{\sigma(0)}$. The boundary-filling assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary], for $r$ and dimension $d$, extends that boundary over $\sigma$ over $h\sigma$. Do this for all cells in that dimension; their overlaps lie in the previous skeleton. At the union take the compatible simplicial maps. This constructs $f$ with both equations exact. Transposition gives $\bar F:J\times S\to E$ over $\operatorname{pr}_S$, extending $F$, hence a join cocone $\bar P:J\to\Gamma(q)$. Its evaluation at $s$ is $x_s$; passing from join cocones to coherent cocones as in Step 1 gives the required cocone $C$ with each evaluation equivalent to $c_s$.

source.place: Agent-written skeletal assembly, using Kerodon 7.1.5.17(3) and the relative skeletal filtration in the proof of 1.5.5.14(b).

proof.text: The vertex $f$ is initial in $Z$. To prove it, apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $Z\to\Delta^0$. A boundary $\partial\Delta^n\to Z$, $n>0$, with first vertex $f$ is a map $\partial\Delta^n\times S\to X$ over $h\operatorname{pr}_S$. Extend it across $\Delta^n\times S$ using the relative skeletal filtration of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]. Every missing simplex has surjective projection onto $\Delta^n$; otherwise its image lies in a proper face and it was already in $\partial\Delta^n\times S$. Thus its dimension is positive and its first vertex lies in $\{0\}\times S$. Its lifted first vertex is $f(s)=x_s$, which is $r$-initial. The same boundary-filling lemma for $r$ fills each cell, keeping the entire boundary and base fixed. This supplies the requested simplex in $Z$, so $f$ is initial. By the exponential law for simplicial maps, $Z$ is exactly the category of join cocones on $P$ in $\Gamma(q)$ with boundary $P$ fixed. The fixed-boundary comparison in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], dualized using [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4), identifies it with the coherent cocone category. Equivalences preserve initial objects because they induce equivalences on mapping spaces [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Therefore $C$ is colimiting in $\Gamma(q)$. Notice that this proof applies to any $f$ over $h$ whose vertices are $r$-initial, not just to the particular lift constructed in Step 3.

source.place: Agent-written product-skeleton argument using Kerodon 7.1.5.17(3), 1.5.5.14(b), and 4.6.4.9, colimit dual.

proof.text: Let $D$ be any coherent cocone on $P$ whose evaluations $d_s$ are colimiting. Both $d_s$ and $c_s$ are initial in the coherent cocone category of $P_s$; by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] they are equivalent there. Applying $a_!$ preserves this equivalence of cocones, so $a_!d_s$ is equivalent to the colimiting $a_!c_s$ and is colimiting by the same mapping-space criterion. Choose a join representative of $D$ with boundary $P$, using the fixed-boundary comparison and opposite duality as in Step 1, now in the quasicategory $\Gamma(q)$. Each evaluated join cocone is a $q$-colimit by [lem-coef-local-fiber-relative-colimit-test], and therefore an $r$-initial object by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-initial-corner]. Its transpose is an object of $Z$. The argument of Step 4 makes that object initial in $Z$ and hence makes $D$ colimiting. This proves the pointwise-to-section implication without requiring preservation of any colimits other than the specified transports.

source.place: HTT 4.3.1.10; uniqueness of initial objects and the explicit argument of Step 4.

proof.text: Conversely, let $D$ be colimiting in $\Gamma(q)$. The cocones $C$ and $D$ are initial in the same coherent cocone category, so [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] supplies an equivalence between them. Evaluation at $s$ is a simplicial functor on cocone categories and therefore carries that equivalence, including its two inverse witnesses, to an equivalence of cocones on $P_s$. Since $C_s$ is equivalent to $c_s$, the mapping-space cocone criterion makes $D_s$ colimiting. Together with Step 5 this proves the stated equivalence. If $K$ is empty, the same argument uses relative-initial objects and $J=\Delta^0$; if $S$ is empty, all the lifting problems have empty product and the section category is terminal. No contractibility of $K$, cocompleteness of any fiber, colimit in $S$, or global cocartesian-fibration condition was used.

source.place: Uniqueness of initial objects (Kerodon 4.7.3.14, opposite dual for cocones) and the cocone mapping-space criterion.

proof_origin.place: Explicit relative-initial boundary and product-skeleton proof of the colimit dual of HA 3.2.2.9, specialized to sections after HTT 4.3.1.10. HA, HTT and Kerodon archives are WANTED; sources were read online.
